title: dombeya ambalabeensis subsp. analavelonae
intro: Dombeya ambalabeensis subsp. analavelonae, commonly known as Analavelona, is a plant species in the family Malvaceae. It is used in traditional medicine in Madagascar, where it is valued for its diverse health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antimalarial properties. The bioactive constituents of Analavelona include flavonoids, alkaloids, and terpenoids, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antiparasitic effects. The plant is traditionally used to treat various ailments, including malaria, fever, and respiratory infections, and its therapeutic actions are attributed to its ability to inhibit the growth of pathogens and reduce inflammation.
